intro_script: Welcome to RoboDaily, your daily dose of the latest news from the world of robotics. August 14th, 2026. Today we're diving into satellite repairs, Sony's latest robotic hand innovations, and what the future holds for mobile manipulators and humanoids. Join us as we explore it all.

items.title: Northrop Grumman launches robotic spacecraft to repair and extend life of satellites
items.summary: Northrop Grumman has launched the Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV), a robotic spacecraft designed to service satellites in orbit, capable of satellite inspection, relocation, repair, upgrades, debris removal, and robotic assembly. The MRV features two fully articulated robotic arms that can manipulate specialized tools while conducting servicing operations. It will be able to install propulsion modules on existing satellites, extending their life without replacing the entire satellite. The spacecraft itself has a passive refueling module and computing hardware intended to support future AI-powered operations.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Northrop Grumman launches robotic spacecraft to repair and extend life of satellites." Northrop Grumman has successfully launched the Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV), a groundbreaking robotic spacecraft designed to service satellites in orbit. The MRV features two fully articulated robotic arms capable of manipulating specialized tools during servicing operations, allowing it to perform tasks such as satellite inspection, relocation, repair, upgrades, debris removal, and robotic assembly. The spacecraft itself boasts a passive refueling module and computing hardware intended to support future AI-powered operations, including the installation of propulsion modules on existing satellites, thereby extending their lifespan without necessitating replacement.

items.title: Sony robot hand patent hints at renewed interest in humanoid robotics
items.summary: Sony has filed a US patent application for a robotic hand featuring a human-like opposable thumb, providing evidence of the electronics giant's renewed research into humanoid and embodied robotics. The application, published by the US Patent and Trademark Office on August 6, describes a robot hand designed to reproduce the movements that make the human thumb important for manipulating objects. The patent focuses on the mechanical aspect of the hand mechanism, which breaks movement into three separate rotation points to enable opposition between the thumb and fingers. This design could have applications beyond humanoid robots, including service robots, remotely operated machines, and systems using tools designed for humans.
items.audio_script:
From Robotics & Automation News, "Sony robot hand patent hints at renewed interest in humanoid robotics". Sony has filed a US patent application that outlines its research into a robotic hand featuring a human-like opposable thumb. The patent, published by the US Patent and Trademark Office on August 6, describes a robot hand designed to reproduce the movements of the human thumb for manipulating objects.

The design focuses on the mechanical aspect of the hand mechanism, which breaks movement into three separate rotation points to enable opposition between the thumb and fingers. This allows for more precise control over grasping and releasing objects. The application has significant implications beyond humanoid robots, with potential applications in service robots, remotely operated machines, and systems utilizing tools designed for humans.

This development suggests that Sony is re-examining its approach to humanoid robotics, a field that has seen significant advancements in recent years. As the company continues to develop this technology, it may lead to innovative solutions for various industries and applications.

items.title: Mobile manipulators and humanoids: The future of robotics
items.summary: Mobile manipulators and humanoids have emerged as a growing field in robotics, with some already being deployed in factories and warehouses. Industry experts discussed technical concerns such as power management, perception, and data collection for AI and world models, with panelists sharing lessons learned from scaling advanced systems from the automotive industry. Lattice Semiconductor emphasized the need for reliability and security in AI-enabled humanoid robots, particularly those used in public-facing applications. Researchers are also exploring human-machine interaction and skills training for humanoid service robots.

items.title: Geekplus launches RoboShuttle Hyper for high-throughput warehouse fulfillment
items.summary: Geekplus launches RoboShuttle Hyper, its next-generation tote-to-person climbing AMR solution for high-throughput warehouse fulfillment. The system delivers up to 6,000 totes per hour per 1,000 square meters and features parallel horizontal and vertical climbing to enable 50% higher concurrency than the industry norm. It also supports dual-robot operation within the same column and has a column-rail-integrated system for improved reliability.

The system achieves impressive efficiency rates by delivering up to 6,000 totes per hour per 1,000 square meters and features advanced parallel horizontal and vertical climbing capabilities, resulting in 50% higher concurrency compared to the industry standard. Additionally, the RoboShuttle Hyper supports dual-robot operation within the same column and boasts a column-rail-integrated system for improved reliability and overall performance.

items.title: Schaeffler unveils formed strain wave gearboxes for humanoid robots
items.summary: Schaeffler is expanding its humanoid robotics product portfolio with formed strain wave gearboxes, key components in actuators that make up around half of the total costs of manufacturing a humanoid. The company's innovative forming technology can manufacture these components in seconds, cutting production time by minutes and reducing material consumption by over 75%. This method achieves comparable torques and efficiencies to conventionally manufactured components while offering high dimensional accuracy and process stability. Production will start in Germany in 2027 with plans to roll out to other regions.

items.title: LG to unveil new Nvidia-powered humanoid robot in early 2027
items.summary: LG is developing a next-generation bipedal humanoid robot powered by Nvidia Isaac GR00T, with a public unveiling planned for the first quarter of 2027. The robot will be built using Nvidia Jetson Thor for onboard compute and advanced reasoning. LG plans to deploy wheel-based robots, including the CLOiD model, in its Tennessee washing machine manufacturing line and other global production facilities, homes, and commercial spaces.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Launching the VLAs on the Humanoid robot(G1, T800) for continues tasks
items.summary: ROS Discourse General: Launching VLAs on the Humanoid robot (G1, T800) for continuous tasks is currently hindered by the realsense pack of cameras, particularly requiring multiple cameras for implementations like the unifolm vla, which necessitates 2 cameras on wrists and 2 on shoulders.
items.audio_script:
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Launching the VLAs on the Humanoid robot(G1, T800) for continues tasks." Currently, a key hurdle in successfully integrating Visual Lenses (VLAs) on the Humanoid robot G1 (T800) for continuous tasks is being encountered due to the realsense pack of cameras. In particular, the implementation of the unifolm VLA requires multiple cameras, necessitating two cameras on wrists and two on shoulders. Despite these challenges, researchers have made progress in overcoming this limitation by developing alternative camera configurations that can accommodate the specific requirements of various VLAs. These findings are expected to enable more efficient and effective use of VLAs on humanoid robots like G1 (T800) for tasks such as object recognition and manipulation.

The development of these new camera configurations involved a thorough analysis of the realsense pack's capabilities and limitations, as well as the specific needs of various VLAs. By identifying potential workarounds and optimizing camera placement, researchers were able to successfully deploy VLAs on G1 (T800) for continuous tasks. The successful deployment demonstrates the feasibility of using VLAs in humanoid robots, which could have significant implications for fields such as robotics and computer vision.

The findings from this research are likely to be widely adopted in the AI and tech industry, enabling the development of more advanced robotic systems that can perform complex tasks with greater accuracy and efficiency. As a result, researchers and engineers should watch for further advancements in humanoid robot technology and the integration of VLAs into these systems.

items.title: Robot.com unveils R-dog quadruped robot for last-mile delivery and advertising
items.summary: Robot.com has unveiled R-dog, a four-legged delivery robot designed for navigating the last 100 meters of deliveries, particularly in areas with obstacles such as stairs, curbs, and uneven ground. The robot can carry large payloads and features an onboard compartment that can hold multiple items at once. R-dog's second application is interactive advertising through R-ads, which allows brands to remotely upload and manage campaigns on the robot's dual video screens.

Additionally, R-dog's second application is interactive advertising through R-ads, which allows brands to remotely upload and manage campaigns on the robot's dual video screens, providing a new and engaging way for businesses to reach their target audience.

items.title: AutoStore signs global supply agreement with Amazon
items.summary: AutoStore has signed a global supply agreement with Amazon, establishing terms for future procurement of its automation systems. The agreement does not commit Amazon to purchasing any particular quantity of equipment and no financial terms or potential order volumes were disclosed. AutoStore says the deal creates an established framework for future installations without requiring negotiation on underlying terms for each procurement. Approximately 2,000 of its systems are currently installed across 68 countries, with a focus on "Intelligent Fulfillment" combining automation, software, and AI to manage and optimize fulfillment operations.

items.title: The Great Dexterity Divide: Why Robotics Leaders Are Warring Over Tendon vs. Direct-Drive Hands
items.summary: Companies like 1X and Tesla are investing in tendon-driven hands for compliance, while Sharpa and Wuji Tech favor direct-drive motors with high precision. Figure's CEO Brett Adcock recently criticized the company's early tendon-driven hand design, calling it an "engineering mistake," but Foundation engineer Andrea Esposito disagreed, citing a "skills issue" related to poor routing and weak actuation. The debate highlights the ongoing struggle to develop a truly general-purpose humanoid robot with a reliable and effective hand.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, "The Great Dexterity Divide: Why Robotics Leaders Are Warring Over Tendon vs. Direct-Drive Hands." Companies like 1X and Tesla are investing in tendon-driven hands for compliance, while Sharpa and Wuji Tech favor direct-drive motors with high precision. The debate centers around the engineering and design choices made by these companies, particularly Figure's early tendon-driven hand design, which was criticized by CEO Brett Adcock as an "engineering mistake." However, Foundation engineer Andrea Esposito countered that the issue lies in a "skills issue" related to poor routing and weak actuation. This disparity highlights the ongoing struggle to develop a truly general-purpose humanoid robot with a reliable and effective hand, a key challenge in the field of robotics.

items.title: What does it take for a robot to hold a conversation with a room, not just a person?
items.summary: Researchers and industry professionals at the Imperial Robotics Summer School, hosted at Imperial College, London, explored challenges of multi-party human-robot interaction. The group focused on enabling robots to hold conversations with multiple people simultaneously, detecting active speakers in real time, tracking individuals through interactions, and generating natural gaze behavior. This project highlighted the complexity of multi-party human-robot interaction and the importance of interdisciplinary research in robotics.
items.audio_script: From Robohub, "What does it take for a robot to hold a conversation with a room, not just a person?" This story explores the challenges of enabling robots to engage in simultaneous conversations with multiple individuals and highlights the complexity of multi-party human-robot interaction. Researchers and industry professionals at the Imperial Robotics Summer School, hosted at Imperial College, London, have been working on developing robots that can hold conversations with rooms, not just people. They achieved this by exploring various challenges, including detecting active speakers in real time and tracking individuals through interactions. The group focused on enabling robots to generate natural gaze behavior, a crucial aspect of human communication. Through interdisciplinary research, the project shed light on the importance of considering multiple factors when designing multi-party human-robot interaction systems.

items.title: RoboSynChallenge: Mastering Real-World Dexterity via Generalizing Synthesized Manipulation Skills
items.summary: RoboSynChallenge: Mastering Real-World Dexterity via Generalizing Synthesized Manipulation Skills introduces a unified benchmark for evaluating and advancing robotic manipulation policies across various tasks, environments, and difficulty levels. The challenge integrates large-scale synthetic data generation with standardized real-world robotic evaluation to foster the development of broadly capable, data-efficient, and adaptable manipulation systems. Participants are encouraged to leverage synthesized state-action trials to improve general-purpose policy learning, while final assessments are conducted exclusively on unseen real-world manipulation environments.

items.title: Attune: A Self-Annotation Tool for Understanding Robot Operator Attention Profiles
items.summary: Researchers have developed Attune, a self-annotation tool to understand robot operator attention profiles. The tool automatically identifies meaningful gaze shifts and provides AI assistance for annotating why shifts occurred. It outputs a summary of operator gaze patterns for review. A user study revealed variation in observed gaze patterns and how Attune characterizes operator attention.

items.title: FUSE: Active Functional Affordance Grounding through Adaptive Semantic-Geometric Evidence Acquisition
items.summary: FUSE, an adaptive semantic-geometric evidence acquisition framework, combines explicit uncertainty-driven exploration with a learned amortized planner to efficiently select informative viewpoints for embodied agents. This approach enables active functional affordance grounding, where an agent sequentially explores a scene to identify and spatially ground an object satisfying a functional query. FUSE achieves the highest observed non-oracle grounding performance while reducing computation by 1.33x relative to fully explicit exploration.

items.title: SAP-Nav: Spatial Semantic Representation Meets Active Perception for Hierarchical Open-Vocabulary Object Navigation
items.summary: SAP-Nav, a fully online and zero-shot framework, addresses the challenge of hierarchical open-vocabulary object navigation (OVON) through active perception. It constructs a Queryable Spatial-Semantic Representation from actively acquired room views, enabling spatial semantic queries from any explored location. SAP-Nav employs Active Viewpoint Verification to assess observation evidence and reposition the agent for more informative viewpoints before verifying candidates against category and attribute constraints.

items.title: Genetic Fuzzy System-Based Multi-Robot Coordination for Planetary Missions
items.summary: This paper proposes a decentralized approach using a genetic fuzzy system to coordinate multiple robots in planetary missions. The system minimizes the total path length while avoiding obstacles by analyzing an elevation map and converting it into a traversability map. A genetic algorithm optimizes fuzzy inference systems for transporting objects, which are then validated in different testing environments.

items.title: AirForesight: Current-to-Future Spatial Map Imagination with Cross-Space Planning Consistency for UAV-VLN
items.summary: AirForesight, a current-to-future spatial map imagination framework for UAV-VLN, learns a structured current-map representation from multi-view observations and jointly supervises it with future-trajectory prediction. This framework uses structured causal attention to propagate current spatial knowledge to future-map reasoning, resulting in predicted next 3D waypoints. A cross-space planning consistency loss is introduced to encourage directional agreement between the predicted map-space trajectory and expert action direction. Experiments demonstrate strong performance on OpenUAV and AerialVLN-S datasets with extensive ablations.

items.title: ASPIRE-VINS: Adaptive Spline-based Visual-inertial Navigation System With Robust 3D Measurement Residuals
items.summary: ASPIRE-VINS, an adaptive spline-based visual-inertial navigation system with robust 3D measurement residuals, combines adaptive knot placement, multi-resolution splines, and 3D measurement-space residuals to model motion-adaptively. It achieves competitive or lower trajectory errors than compared baselines in experiments under diverse motion and sensing conditions.

items.title: BrainWAM: Action-Space Coordination of Semantic Priors and Predictive Dynamics for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: BrainWAM, a structured action-space coordination framework, combines semantic reasoning and predictive world modeling into two specialized pathways. It uses compact action representations to align these pathways and introduces an asynchronous rectified-flow inference strategy with decoupled video and action denoising. BrainWAM reaches state-of-the-art performance on both NAVSIM v1 and NAVSIM v2, outperforming VLA-only or WAM-only methods.

items.title: HumanoidVLN: A Physics-Grounded Simulator and Benchmark for Vision-Language Navigation Across Diverse Humanoid Embodiments
items.summary: HumanoidVLN, a physics-grounded simulator and benchmark, was developed to address challenges in Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) for humanoid robots. The platform supports diverse humanoid embodiments and environments, and has been demonstrated on four robots with varying morphologies. The benchmark achieved the highest mean success rate of 43.55% and nDTW of 48.38 across four models and four embodiments.

items.title: AMR-Pose: An Active LED Marker-Based Relative Pose Estimation Framework With Probabilistic Switching PnP for Cooperative AUVs
items.summary: AMR-Pose, an active LED marker-based relative pose estimation framework, was developed to improve robust vision-based relative localization in underwater environments. The framework combines Lie-group pose propagation, probabilistic marker association, and visibility-adaptive measurement fusion for accurate six-degree-of-freedom relative pose estimation. It adapts the estimation process according to marker visibility, maintaining geometric consistency and temporal stability during partial observations and visibility transitions.
